_comment: A RATCHET, not an exemption. It records how many x-arthome-vocabulary blocks
in openapi/*.yaml still carry no x-arthome-vocabulary-source, so the gate can
be useful TODAY on contracts that are not annotated yet.
Two properties make it a ratchet and not a truce:
- the number may go DOWN, never up. New drift fails immediately, because a
new block without a source pushes the count above the allowance.
- it EXPIRES. `removeAfter` is read by the gate, which turns red once the
date has passed. An allowance without a deadline is a permanent exemption
that does not say its name (code-conventions.md 7.6).
`rebaselineAfter` dates the SLACK separately, so an allowance set above the
real count cannot stay there quietly.
SET FROM A MEASUREMENT, NEVER FROM A PREDICTION — and this file learned that
the hard way. It was first set to 148: the count was 143 because five blocks
were unparseable (the YAML boolean trap), and 148 was a PREDICTION of what the
count would become once they were quoted. They were quoted, the real count was
149, and the gate went red for FIXING a defect — the one thing a ratchet must
never do. The prediction was off by one because the contracts had gained a
block in the meantime, which is exactly the kind of thing a prediction cannot
see.
So: when a fix changes the count, re-baseline in the SAME commit as the fix.
Do not calibrate an allowance against a future you have not observed.
Lower `undeclaredAllowed` as blocks get annotated. When it reaches 0, delete
this file.
why: 149 of 149 blocks are unannotated: the x-arthome-vocabulary-source key was introduced with the gate itself, on 2026-09-22. Annotating them is backend-contracts' work.
